title: Gluing local immersions representing a source-local predicate
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. For each morphism $g:T\to S$ let $P(g)$ be a proposition. Suppose $P(g)$ implies $P(g\circ h)$ for every $h:T'\to T$, and suppose $P(g)$ holds whenever every point of $T$ has an open neighbourhood $V$ with $P(g\circ\iota_V)$. Assume that for each $s\in S$ there exist an open neighbourhood $U$, a scheme $W_U$, and an immersion $j_U:W_U\to U$ representing the predicate: for all $g:T\to U$, $g$ factors through $j_U$ if and only if $P(\iota_U\circ g)$. Then there exist a scheme $W$ and an immersion $j:W\to S$ with, for all $g:T\to S$, $g$ factors through $j$ if and only if $P(g)$.

proof.text: Choose the neighbourhood and local representative at each s. They cover S. Pull back each representative to overlaps. Base-change stability and the representing criteria show that both overlap restrictions represent P on the overlap. Apply each criterion to the other representative to obtain inverse arrows. Immersions are monomorphisms, so these inverses and their triple-overlap compatibility follow by cancellation.

The overlaps are open subschemes of the representatives, being inverse images of open neighbourhoods in S. The unique overlap isomorphisms give cocycle gluing data. Glue the schemes and their compatible maps to S. Its restriction over each neighbourhood is the original immersion. The Mathlib target-locality instance for IsImmersion implies that the glued map is an immersion.

If P(g) holds, base-change stability gives P on the inverse-image cover of T. The local criteria give factors through the corresponding open pieces of W. Monomorphy of j makes them agree on overlaps; open-cover gluing gives a global factor. Conversely, if g factors through W, pull it back to that inverse-image cover; each local representing criterion gives P there. Source locality gives P(g). For empty S the empty gluing family is used, and for empty T source locality applies to its vacuous pointwise cover.
